courses.subject: ELA
courses.title: ELA 1
courses.description: First-grade English Language Arts builds strong readers through systematic phonics (short vowels, digraphs, blends, silent e, vowel teams, r-controlled vowels, diphthongs, syllables), fluency practice, and rich read-alouds of classic and public-domain literature such as Frog and Toad, Aesop's Fables, Beatrix Potter and Robert Louis Stevenson. Students write narratives, informative reports and opinion pieces, and grow grammar, vocabulary, speaking and listening skills every week.
courses.framework: California Common Core State Standards for ELA/Literacy; 2014 CA ELA/ELD Framework

standards.RL.1.1: Ask and answer questions about key details in a story.
standards.RL.1.2: Retell stories, including key details, and demonstrate understanding of their central message or lesson.
standards.RL.1.3: Describe characters, settings, and major events in a story, using key details.
standards.RL.1.4: Identify words and phrases in stories or poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.
standards.RL.1.5: Explain major differences between books that tell stories and books that give information.
standards.RL.1.6: Identify who is telling the story at various points in a text.
standards.RL.1.7: Use illustrations and details in a story to describe its characters, setting, or events.
standards.RL.1.9: Compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in stories.
standards.RL.1.10: With prompting and support, read prose and poetry of appropriate complexity for grade 1.
standards.RI.1.1: Ask and answer questions about key details in an informational text.
standards.RI.1.2: Identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.
standards.RI.1.3: Describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.
standards.RI.1.4: Ask and answer questions to determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases in a text.
standards.RI.1.5: Know and use text features (headings, tables of contents, glossaries, icons) to locate facts.
standards.RI.1.6: Distinguish between information provided by pictures or illustrations and information provided by the words.
standards.RI.1.7: Use the illustrations and details in a text to describe its key ideas.
standards.RI.1.8: Identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.
standards.RI.1.9: Identify basic similarities and differences between two texts on the same topic.
standards.RI.1.10: With prompting and support, read informational texts appropriately complex for grade 1.
standards.RF.1.1a: Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence (first word, capitalization, ending punctuation).
standards.RF.1.2a: Distinguish long from short vowel sounds in spoken single-syllable words.
standards.RF.1.2b: Orally produce single-syllable words by blending sounds, including consonant blends.
standards.RF.1.2c: Isolate and pronounce initial, medial vowel, and final sounds in spoken single-syllable words.
standards.RF.1.2d: Segment spoken single-syllable words into their complete sequence of individual sounds.
standards.RF.1.3a: Know the spelling-sound correspondences for common consonant digraphs.
standards.RF.1.3c: Know final -e and common vowel team conventions for representing long vowel sounds.
standards.RF.1.3d: Use knowledge that every syllable must have a vowel sound to determine the number of syllables in a printed word.
standards.RF.1.3e: Decode two-syllable words following basic patterns by breaking the words into syllables.
standards.RF.1.3g: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
standards.RF.1.4a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
standards.RF.1.4b: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
standards.RF.1.4c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
standards.W.1.1: Write opinion pieces that introduce the topic, state an opinion, supply a reason, and provide closure.
standards.W.1.2: Write informative/explanatory texts that name a topic, supply facts, and provide closure.
standards.W.1.3: Write narratives recounting two or more sequenced events with details, temporal words, and closure.
standards.W.1.5: With guidance, focus on a topic, respond to questions and suggestions, and add details to strengthen writing.
standards.W.1.6: With guidance, use digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.
standards.W.1.7: Participate in shared research and writing projects.
standards.W.1.8: With guidance, recall information from experiences or gather information from sources to answer a question.
standards.SL.1.1: Participate in collaborative conversations, following agreed-upon rules, building on others' talk, and asking questions.
standards.SL.1.2: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text read aloud or information presented orally or through media.
standards.SL.1.3: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says to gather information or clarify something not understood.
standards.SL.1.4: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas and feelings clearly.
standards.SL.1.4a: Memorize and recite poems, rhymes, and songs with expression (CA addition).
standards.SL.1.5: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions when appropriate to clarify ideas.
standards.SL.1.6: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation.
standards.L.1.1a: Print all upper- and lowercase letters.
standards.L.1.1b: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.
standards.L.1.1c: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in basic sentences.
standards.L.1.1d: Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns.
standards.L.1.1e: Use verbs to convey a sense of past, present, and future.
standards.L.1.1g: Use frequently occurring conjunctions (and, but, or, so, because).
standards.L.1.1j: Produce and expand complete simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences.
standards.L.1.2a: Capitalize dates and names of people.
standards.L.1.2c: Use commas in dates and to separate single words in a series.
standards.L.1.2d: Use conventional spelling for words with common spelling patterns and frequently occurring irregular words.
standards.L.1.2e: Spell untaught words phonetically, drawing on phonemic awareness and spelling conventions.
standards.L.1.4a: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
standards.L.1.4b: Use frequently occurring affixes as a clue to the meaning of a word.
standards.L.1.4c: Identify frequently occurring root words and their inflectional forms.
standards.L.1.5a: Sort words into categories to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.
standards.L.1.5b: Define words by category and by one or more key attributes.
standards.L.1.5c: Identify real-life connections between words and their use.
standards.L.1.5d: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs and adjectives differing in manner or intensity.
standards.L.1.6: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, including conjunctions for simple relationships.

units.title: Readers and Writers Begin: Print Concepts & Short Vowels
units.big_idea: Letters stand for sounds, and sentences carry ideas from writer to reader.

units.title: Digraphs and Friendship Stories
units.big_idea: Two letters can work together to make one sound; good readers notice how characters act and feel.

units.title: Consonant Blends and Fables & Folktales
units.big_idea: Stories from long ago teach lessons that still matter today.

units.title: Silent e and Animal Information Books
units.big_idea: Information books teach facts, and text features help us find them.

units.title: Vowel Teams and Poetry
units.big_idea: Poets choose words for sound and feeling; vowel teams help us read long-vowel words.

units.title: R-Controlled Vowels and Opinion Writing
units.big_idea: Writers share opinions and give reasons to convince readers.

units.title: Syllables, Endings and Plant Science Reading
units.big_idea: Big words are made of smaller parts; informational texts on the same topic can be compared.

units.title: Diphthongs and Classic Storybooks

units.big_idea: Readers and writers ask questions, find answers, and share what they learn.

weeks.topic: Print concepts, sentences, and short a
objectives: Identify the parts of a sentence (capital, spaces, end mark)
Blend and read CVC words with short a

days.title: Sentence detectives
days.work: Read aloud 'Hey Diddle Diddle' and point to each word; circle the capital letter and period in three printed sentences.

days.title: Short a sound
days.work: Say /a/ words (cat, map, bag), isolate the middle sound, then build cat, mat, sat, hat with letter tiles and read each one.

days.title: Handwriting a, c, d
days.work: Practice lowercase a, c, d (circle letters) on lined paper; write the CVC words bad, cad, dad.

days.title: Talking rules
days.work: Read 'Chrysanthemum' (Kevin Henkes, library) and practice listening rules: take turns, look at the speaker, ask one question about Chrysanthemum's name.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Read 10 short-a CVC words aloud and write a dictated sentence 'The cat sat.' with capital and period; tally correct sounds.

weeks.assessment: Oral CVC reading check (8/10 correct) and dictated sentence with correct capital and period.

objectives: Read short-i CVC words
Recognize first sight words (the, a, is, I, see, my)
materials: 'The Snowy Day' by Ezra Jack Keats

days.title: Sound boxes
days.work: Push a counter into an Elkonin box for each sound in pig, sit, lip, win; then write the letters in the boxes.

days.title: Sight word cards
days.work: Make flash cards for the, a, is, I, see, my; play 'Go Fish' with them and read sentences like 'I see a pig.'

days.title: Read-aloud questions
days.work: Read 'The Snowy Day' and ask/answer who, what, where questions about Peter's day; draw a favorite part.

days.title: Handwriting i, t, l
days.work: Practice lowercase straight-line letters i, t, l and write tip, lit, it, sit.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Read a short decodable text from Starfall (short a and i), then sort 12 picture cards by middle sound a or i.

weeks.assessment: Picture sort accuracy and fluent reading of 6 sight words.

weeks.topic: Short o and short u; personal narrative start
objectives: Read short o and u words
Tell a story from personal experience in order

days.title: Short o
days.work: Build and read hot, pot, dot, mop, top with tiles; change one letter to make a new word (hot→hop→hip).

days.title: Short u
days.work: Read bug, cup, sun, run, hut; play 'I spy' with short u sounds around the house.

days.title: Characters & setting
days.work: Read 'Owl Moon' and name the characters and setting; draw the snowy woods and label two details.

days.title: Small moment story
days.work: Draw a picture of something you did this summer, then tell the story aloud and write one sentence about it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Mixed short-vowel word read (a, i, o, u) and spelling test of 8 CVC words; reread the small-moment sentence to a family member.

weeks.assessment: Spelling of 8 CVC words and oral retell of a small-moment story with a beginning and end.

weeks.topic: Short e and all short vowels; narrative sentences
objectives: Distinguish all five short vowel sounds
Write a 2–3 sentence personal narrative

days.title: Short e
days.work: Read bed, red, pet, ten, web; segment each word into sounds and spell it with tiles.

days.title: Vowel sort
days.work: Sort 20 word cards into five short-vowel columns, read each column aloud.

days.title: Read Henry and Mudge
days.work: Read the first chapter of 'Henry and Mudge' together; answer questions about how Henry feels and why.

days.title: Write it
days.work: Write a 2–3 sentence story about a pet or animal you know, using first and then; check each sentence for a capital and period.

days.title: Unit 1 check
days.work: Phonics screener of 25 CVC words and 10 sight words; read the narrative aloud and add one detail.

weeks.assessment: Unit 1 phonics screener (CVC + sight words) and a scored 2–3 sentence narrative.

weeks.topic: Digraphs sh and ch; Frog and Toad
objectives: Read words with sh and ch
Describe characters using details
materials: 'Frog and Toad Are Friends' by Arnold Lobel (library)

days.title: sh words
days.work: Learn that s+h says /sh/; read ship, shop, fish, dish, shut and underline the digraph.

days.title: ch words
days.work: Read chip, chat, much, chop, lunch; sort picture cards into sh and ch piles.

days.title: Spring
days.work: Read 'Spring' from Frog and Toad Are Friends; list two words that describe Frog and two that describe Toad.

days.title: Picture clues
days.work: Reread 'Spring' and use the illustrations to tell how Toad feels when he wakes up; write one sentence with a period.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Dictation of 6 sh/ch words and one sentence; oral description of Frog vs. Toad.

weeks.assessment: Dictation accuracy for sh/ch and an oral character description using two details.

weeks.topic: Digraphs th and wh; comparing characters
objectives: Read words with th and wh
Compare two characters' experiences

days.title: th words
days.work: Read thin, this, that, path, bath; feel your tongue for voiced and unvoiced th.

days.title: wh words
days.work: Read when, what, which, whip, whiz; write three question words on cards and ask a family member a question with each.

days.title: The Story
days.work: Read 'The Story' (Frog and Toad); retell what Toad tries in order to think of a story.

days.title: Nouns
days.work: Learn that nouns name people, places, and things; find 6 nouns in 'The Lost Button' and sort into person/place/thing.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Fill a Venn diagram comparing Frog and Toad; read th/wh word list for accuracy.

weeks.assessment: Venn diagram with at least 2 likenesses and 2 differences; th/wh word list read.

weeks.topic: ck, ng, and proper nouns; Frog and Toad Together
objectives: Read words with -ck and -ng
Capitalize proper nouns

days.title: -ck words
days.work: Read duck, back, sick, rock, truck; learn that ck comes right after a short vowel.

days.title: -ng words
days.work: Read sing, ring, long, hung, bang; write a silly sentence using three -ng words.

days.title: A List
days.work: Read 'A List' from Frog and Toad Together; make your own to-do list for tomorrow with 4 items.

days.title: Proper nouns
days.work: Write the names of 5 family members, your street and your town, capitalizing each proper noun.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Read a decodable passage with digraphs; circle common nouns and box proper nouns in 5 sentences.

weeks.assessment: Noun sort worksheet and digraph passage read with 90% accuracy.

objectives: Apply all digraphs in reading and spelling
Write a narrative with two events and a closing
materials: drawing paper stapled into a 4-page booklet

days.title: Digraph game
days.work: Play digraph bingo with sh, ch, th, wh, ck, ng words; read each word you cover.

days.title: Cookies
days.work: Read 'Cookies' (Frog and Toad Together); discuss what willpower means and tell about a time you showed it.

days.title: Plan a story
days.work: Plan a story about doing something with a friend: draw first, next, last pictures in a booklet.

days.title: Write the story
days.work: Write a sentence under each picture using first, next, then, last, and end with how you felt.

days.title: Unit 2 check
days.work: Read the booklet aloud with expression; complete a 20-word digraph reading check.

weeks.assessment: Friendship booklet scored on sequence words, capitals/periods; digraph reading check.

objectives: Blend initial l-blends
Retell a folktale and state its lesson

days.title: l-blends
days.work: Blend and read clap, flag, glad, plum, slip, black; tap each sound.

days.title: Read The Little Red Hen
days.work: Read the folktale aloud; act it out with stuffed animals, repeating 'Not I!'

days.title: Retell
days.work: Retell the story using a 5-finger retell (characters, setting, problem, events, ending).

days.title: Lesson
days.work: Discuss the lesson (people who help get to share); write one sentence telling the lesson.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Spelling of 8 l-blend words; oral retell scored with retell checklist.

objectives: Read words with r-blends
Identify the moral of a fable

days.title: r-blends
days.work: Read crab, drum, frog, grin, trip, brush; sort picture cards by br, cr, dr, fr, gr, tr.

days.title: The Tortoise and the Hare
days.work: Read the fable and discuss why slow and steady won; draw the race with a speech bubble for each animal.

days.title: The Lion and the Mouse
days.work: Read the fable and state its moral (little friends can be great friends) in your own words.

days.title: Past tense -ed
days.work: Read jumped, helped, rested and turn 5 present verbs into past verbs to tell what the hare did.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Read an r-blend passage; match 3 fables to their morals.

weeks.assessment: Fable–moral matching and r-blend passage accuracy.

weeks.topic: S-blends and end blends; Three Billy Goats Gruff
objectives: Read s-blends and final blends (st, nd, mp)
Identify who is telling the story

days.title: s-blends
days.work: Read stop, snap, spin, skip, swim, smell; tap sounds and spell 5 words.

days.title: End blends
days.work: Read nest, hand, jump, milk, tent; underline the final blend in each.

days.title: Who is talking?
days.work: Read Three Billy Goats Gruff; use quotation marks as a clue to who speaks and color each speaker's words a different color.

days.title: Noun-verb match
days.work: Practice 'The goat trips' vs. 'The goats trip'; complete 6 sentences choosing the right verb form.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform the story with stick puppets, changing voices for narrator and each character; blend word check.

weeks.assessment: Puppet show voices for narrator/characters and singular/plural verb sentences.

weeks.topic: Comparing folktales and writing a fable retell
objectives: Compare adventures of characters in two folktales
Write a retelling with beginning, middle, end
materials: 'The Gingerbread Man' and 'The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse' (public domain)

days.title: The Gingerbread Man
days.work: Read the tale; chant the repeating line and list everyone who chased him.

days.title: Town Mouse and Country Mouse
days.work: Read the fable; tell which home you would choose and why.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare the Gingerbread Man and the Country Mouse: where they went, what problems they had, how each ended.

days.title: Write a retell
days.work: Choose a favorite fable and write a 4-sentence retelling with first, next, then, finally, using past-tense verbs.

days.title: Unit 3 check
days.work: Blends assessment (30 words); read your retelling aloud and state the moral.

weeks.assessment: Blends assessment and scored written fable retelling.

weeks.topic: Long a with silent e; what is nonfiction?
objectives: Distinguish long and short a
Tell how storybooks differ from information books
materials: a storybook and an animal information book from the library

days.title: Magic e with a
days.work: Add e to cap, tap, can, mad to make cape, tape, cane, made; read each pair aloud.

days.title: Long or short?
days.work: Listen to 12 spoken words and hold up a short or long card for the vowel sound.

days.title: Fiction or nonfiction
days.work: Compare a storybook with a nonfiction animal book; list 3 differences on a T-chart.

days.title: Ask about facts
days.work: Read a National Geographic Kids 'Frogs' (or similar) book and ask and answer 3 questions about frog facts.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Read 10 a_e words and sort 6 books into fiction and nonfiction with a reason.

weeks.assessment: a_e word reading and fiction/nonfiction sort with reasons.

weeks.topic: Long i and long o with silent e; text features
objectives: Read i_e and o_e words
Use headings, table of contents and glossary
materials: nonfiction animal book with text features

days.title: i_e words
days.work: Read bike, kite, time, ride, five; write them in sentences.

days.title: o_e words
days.work: Read home, rope, bone, nose, stone; play a 'change the vowel' game (hop→hope).

days.title: Text feature hunt
days.work: Use sticky notes to find a table of contents, heading, bold word, and glossary in a nonfiction animal book.

days.title: Adjectives
days.work: Describe an animal photo with 5 adjectives (color, size, feel); write 'The ___ frog is ___.'

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Use the table of contents to find two facts; read an i_e/o_e word list.

weeks.assessment: Text-feature scavenger hunt and long i/o word list.

weeks.topic: Long u and e with silent e; pictures vs. words
objectives: Read u_e and e_e words
Tell what info comes from pictures vs. words
materials: 'Gail Gibbons – Frogs' or another illustrated animal book

days.title: u_e and e_e
days.work: Read cube, tune, mule, these, Pete; mixed silent-e word sort by vowel.

days.title: Main topic
days.work: Read a ReadWorks grade 1 animal passage; name the main topic and two key details.

days.title: Picture vs. words
days.work: Look at a diagram and caption in an animal book; tell one fact you learned from the picture and one from the words.

days.title: Fact cards
days.work: Choose an animal for a mini report; write 3 facts on index cards from a library book.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Silent-e spelling test (10 words); main topic + 2 details organizer.

weeks.assessment: Silent-e spelling test and main-topic organizer.

objectives: Write an informative piece that names a topic, gives facts and a closing
Revise by adding details

days.title: Topic sentence
days.work: Write a topic sentence for your animal report ('Owls are birds that hunt at night.').

days.title: Facts
days.work: Turn 3 fact cards into 3 complete sentences in the report booklet, each with a capital and end mark.

days.title: Closing & diagram
days.work: Write a closing sentence and draw a labeled diagram of the animal with 4 labels.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Read the report to a family member; add one describing adjective to each fact sentence.

days.title: Unit 4 check
days.work: Present the report aloud; long-vowel silent-e reading assessment (20 words).

weeks.assessment: Animal report scored with a simple informative rubric (topic, 3 facts, closing, conventions).

weeks.topic: Vowel teams ai and ay; nursery rhymes and Stevenson
objectives: Read ai and ay words
Identify words that appeal to the senses in poems
materials: 'A Child's Garden of Verses' by Robert Louis Stevenson (Gutenberg)

days.title: ai words
days.work: Read rain, tail, paint, wait, snail; learn 'ai in the middle'.

days.title: ay words
days.work: Read play, day, stay, gray, tray; learn 'ay at the end' and sort ai/ay words.

days.title: Rain
days.work: Read Stevenson's 'Rain' and 'My Shadow'; circle words that help you see or hear something.

days.title: Memorize
days.work: Begin memorizing 'Rain'; copy it into a poetry notebook and illustrate it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Recite 'Rain' with expression; ai/ay word read and spelling.

weeks.topic: Vowel teams ee, ea, and pronouns; poems about feelings
objectives: Read ee and ea words
Use personal and possessive pronouns
materials: pronoun cards (he, she, it, they, his, her, their)

days.title: ee and ea
days.work: Read tree, feet, sleep, eat, sea, leaf; sort and read in phrases.

days.title: Pronouns
days.work: Replace nouns with he, she, it, they in 6 sentences; then use his, her, their.

days.title: Bed in Summer
days.work: Read Stevenson's 'Bed in Summer'; talk about how the child feels and which words show it.

days.title: Shades of meaning
days.work: Line up look, peek, glance, stare (and big, huge, giant) from weakest to strongest and act them out.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: ee/ea dictation; pronoun worksheet; reread 'Bed in Summer' fluently.

weeks.assessment: Pronoun substitution sentences and ee/ea dictation.

weeks.topic: Vowel teams oa, ow, and long-i (ie, igh); writing a poem
objectives: Read oa, ow, ie, igh words
Write a sensory poem
materials: an object to observe (shell, leaf, orange)

days.title: oa and ow
days.work: Read boat, coat, road, snow, grow, slow; build words with vowel-team cards.

days.title: ie and igh
days.work: Read pie, tie, light, night, high; read the phrase 'a bright light at night' three times.

days.title: Five senses
days.work: Observe an orange using all 5 senses; list sensory words on a chart.

days.title: Write a poem
days.work: Write a 5-line senses poem ('I see... I hear... I smell... I touch... I taste...') about the orange.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Vowel-team word list read; perform your senses poem.

weeks.assessment: Senses poem and vowel-team (oa/ow/ie/igh) word read.

objectives: Read poems fluently with expression
Apply all vowel teams

days.title: Mother Goose fluency
days.work: Practice 'Jack and Jill' and 'Hickory Dickory Dock' with a partner, reading with rhythm.

days.title: Fluency routine
days.work: Do three timed repeated readings of a vowel-team decodable passage; graph words correct per minute.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Choose 2 memorized poems; rehearse with gestures and volume.

days.title: Poetry café
days.work: Perform poems for family and record a video; listeners give one compliment.

days.title: Unit 5 check
days.work: Vowel-team assessment (25 words) and fluency check on a cold passage.

weeks.assessment: Vowel-team assessment and words-correct-per-minute fluency baseline.

weeks.topic: ar and or words; what is an opinion?
objectives: Read ar and or words
Tell an opinion and a reason
materials: 'Green Eggs and Ham' by Dr. Seuss (library)

days.title: ar words
days.work: Read car, star, farm, park, shark; write the bossy-r pattern.

days.title: or words
days.work: Read for, corn, horn, storm, fork; sort ar/or picture cards.

days.title: Opinion talk
days.work: Read 'Green Eggs and Ham'; tell whether Sam's friend should have tried them and give a reason using 'because'.

days.title: Opinion sentences
days.work: Write 3 opinion sentences about favorite foods using 'I think... because...'.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: ar/or dictation; share an opinion orally in a complete sentence.

weeks.assessment: ar/or dictation and opinion sentence with 'because'.

weeks.topic: er, ir, ur words; authors' reasons
objectives: Read er, ir, ur words
Identify reasons an author gives
materials: a ReadWorks persuasive/informational passage (e.g., about recycling)
conjunction cards: and, but, or, so, because

days.title: er/ir/ur
days.work: Read her, bird, girl, fur, turn, nurse; learn all three spell the same sound.

days.title: Tricky words
days.work: Practice irregular words (said, were, there, could, would) with a flash-card race.

days.title: Author's reasons
days.work: Read a short passage on why we should recycle; underline two reasons the author gives.

days.title: Conjunctions
days.work: Join sentence pairs with and, but, or, so; write 4 compound sentences.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: er/ir/ur sort; name the author's point and two reasons.

weeks.assessment: Author's point/reasons organizer and conjunction sentences.

weeks.topic: Planning an opinion piece; commas in a series
objectives: Plan an opinion piece with a reason and closing
Use commas in a series and in dates
materials: opinion graphic organizer (OREO: Opinion, Reason, Example, Opinion)

days.title: Commas in a series
days.work: Write lists of three things ('I like red, blue, and green.') using commas.

days.title: Commas in dates
days.work: Write today's date, your birthday, and a holiday date with commas.

days.title: Read two books
days.work: Read two library books (e.g., 'Mercy Watson' and 'Elephant and Piggie'); choose your favorite.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Fill in an OREO organizer: your opinion, two reasons, an example, and a closing.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Comma check (5 sentences); read your organizer to a listener.

weeks.topic: Writing, revising and sharing an opinion piece
objectives: Draft an opinion piece
Revise with feedback

days.title: Draft
days.work: Write the opinion piece from the organizer: opinion sentence, two reasons with 'because', closing.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Listen to a family member's question and add one more detail or reason.

days.title: Edit
days.work: Use a checklist to fix capitals, end marks, commas and spelling of r-controlled words.

days.title: Publish
days.work: Copy neatly and illustrate; read it aloud as a 'book review'.

days.title: Unit 6 check
days.work: R-controlled vowel assessment (24 words) and opinion piece rubric score.

weeks.assessment: Opinion writing rubric and r-controlled vowel assessment.

weeks.topic: Syllables and compound words; plant life cycle text

Read compound words

bean seeds and a zip bag with wet paper towel

days.title: Clap syllables
days.work: Clap and count syllables in names and objects; find the vowel in each syllable.

days.title: Compound words
days.work: Read sunset, rainbow, backpack, cupcake; split them and draw both parts.

days.title: Seed to plant
days.work: Read 'From Seed to Plant'; start a bean in a wet paper towel bag and draw it.

days.title: How things connect
days.work: Explain how a seed connects to a flower using the book's pictures; order 4 life-cycle cards.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Syllable count of 12 printed words; retell the plant life cycle in order.

weeks.topic: Two-syllable words; comparing two plant texts

Compare two texts on the same topic

days.work: Split two-syllable words between consonants (rab-bit, nap-kin, kit-ten, muf-fin) and read them.

days.title: Second text

days.title: Compare
days.work: Make a chart of what both texts say about seeds and what only one says.

days.work: Measure your bean sprout and add a dated sentence to a class-style observation journal.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Read 12 two-syllable words; complete the same/different chart.

weeks.topic: Inflectional endings -s, -ed, -ing; prefixes un- and re-

days.title: -ing

days.title: un- and re-

days.title: Review & check

Write an informative book with facts and pictures

days.title: Write pages

days.title: Finish pages

days.title: Share

days.title: Unit 7 check

weeks.topic: Diphthongs ou/ow; The Tale of Peter Rabbit

Describe characters, setting, events

days.title: Prepositions

days.title: Peter Rabbit, part 2

days.title: Review & check

days.title: au and aw

days.title: Two duck stories
days.work: Read 'Make Way for Ducklings' and 'The Ugly Duckling'; compare the ducks' journeys on a chart.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Vowel-sound word list read; state the central message of 'The Ugly Duckling'.

objectives: Write a narrative with two or more sequenced events, details and an ending
Use temporal words

days.title: Revise & edit
days.work: Add prepositional phrases for where things happened; fix capitals and end marks.

days.title: Unit 8 check
days.work: Diphthong/vowel-sound assessment and narrative rubric score; read the story aloud.

weeks.topic: Shared research: asking and answering questions

Gather information from books and an expert

days.title: Read sources

days.title: Interview

days.title: Organize

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Tell answers to your questions using sources; name where each fact came from.

Speak in complete sentences

days.title: Review & check

Read grade-level text with understanding

days.title: Poppleton

days.title: Real-life words
days.work: Find words around the house that are cozy, bright, or noisy and use them in sentences.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Math 1
courses.description: First-grade mathematics develops fluency with addition and subtraction within 10 and strategies within 20, solving story problems of every type, and understanding the equal sign. Students learn place value (tens and ones) to 120, add and subtract within 100, measure length with units, tell time to the half hour, identify coins, organize data, and reason about shapes and equal shares.
courses.framework: California Common Core State Standards for Mathematics; 2023 CA Mathematics Framework

standards.1.OA.A.1: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems (adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, comparing, unknowns in all positions).
standards.1.OA.A.2: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is 20 or less.
standards.1.OA.B.3: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract (commutative, associative).
standards.1.OA.B.4: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem.
standards.1.OA.C.5: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (counting on 2 to add 2).
standards.1.OA.C.6: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency within 10, using strategies such as making ten, decomposing, and doubles.
standards.1.OA.D.7: Understand the meaning of the equal sign and determine whether equations are true or false.
standards.1.OA.D.8: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers.
standards.1.NBT.A.1: Count to 120, starting at any number less than 120; read and write numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.
standards.1.NBT.B.2: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones (10 as a bundle of ten ones; 11–19; decade numbers).
standards.1.NBT.B.3: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording with >, =, <.
standards.1.NBT.C.4: Add within 100, including a two-digit and a one-digit number and a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using models and strategies.
standards.1.NBT.C.5: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less without counting.
standards.1.NBT.C.6: Subtract multiples of 10 in the range 10–90 from multiples of 10, using models and strategies.
standards.1.MD.A.1: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.
standards.1.MD.A.2: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units by laying multiple copies of a shorter object end to end.
standards.1.MD.B.3: Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.
standards.1.MD.B.3a: Recognize and identify coins, their names, and their value (CA addition).
standards.1.MD.C.4: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the data.
standards.1.G.A.1: Distinguish between defining attributes and non-defining attributes of shapes; build and draw shapes with defining attributes.
standards.1.G.A.2: Compose two-dimensional or three-dimensional shapes to create a composite shape, and compose new shapes from the composite shape.
standards.1.G.A.3: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares; describe shares using halves, fourths, quarters.

units.title: Numbers to 20 and Meanings of Addition & Subtraction
units.big_idea: Counting tells how many; adding joins and subtracting separates.

units.title: Addition and Subtraction Facts within 10
units.big_idea: Facts within 10 can be found with patterns and related to one another.

units.title: Story Problems and the Equal Sign
units.big_idea: The equal sign means 'the same as'; story problems can have an unknown in any spot.

units.title: Adding and Subtracting within 20
units.big_idea: Making ten and doubles make bigger facts easy.

units.title: Data: Sorting, Graphing and Asking Questions
units.big_idea: Data organized into categories helps us answer questions.

units.title: Place Value: Tens and Ones to 120
units.big_idea: Ten ones make one ten; a digit's place shows its value.

units.title: Adding and Subtracting within 100
units.big_idea: We add tens to tens and ones to ones, and sometimes make a new ten.

units.title: Measuring Length
units.big_idea: Length is measured by repeating equal units end to end with no gaps or overlaps.

units.title: Time and Money
units.big_idea: Clocks show the hour and half hour; coins have different values.

units.title: Geometry: Shapes and Equal Shares
units.big_idea: Shapes are defined by attributes and can be combined or split into equal parts.

units.title: Year Review and Fluency Celebration
units.big_idea: Everything we learned connects: number sense, operations, measurement, and shapes.

objectives: Count objects to 20 and write numerals
Count on from any number

days.title: Count collections
days.work: Count bags of 8–20 beans, organizing them on ten-frames, and write the numeral on a sticky note.

days.title: Write numerals
days.work: Practice writing 0–20 correctly; fix reversals of 2, 3, 5, 7, 9 with tracing and a 'start at the top' rule.

days.title: Count on
days.work: Start at a number on the 0–20 number line (e.g., 7) and count on 3; play 'Start at ___, count on ___'.

days.title: Quick images
days.work: Look at a dot or ten-frame card for 3 seconds and tell how many; explain how you saw it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Count 3 collections, write numerals 0–20 from dictation, and count on from 5 numbers.

weeks.assessment: Counting interview (collections up to 20) and numeral dictation.

weeks.topic: Adding as putting together and adding to
objectives: Represent addition with objects, drawings and equations
Use + and =

days.title: Put together
days.work: Act out 'I have 4 red apples and 3 green apples' with counters and write 4 + 3 = 7.

days.title: Add to
days.work: Solve 'add to' stories (5 birds, 2 more come) with drawings; write the equation.

days.title: Count on to add
days.work: Add by counting on from the bigger number (6 + 2: 'six... seven, eight').

days.title: Shake and spill
days.work: Shake 6 two-color counters, spill, and record all the addition combinations for 6.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Solve 6 picture story problems and write an equation for each.

weeks.topic: Subtracting as taking from and taking apart
objectives: Represent subtraction with objects and equations
Count back to subtract

days.title: Take from
days.work: Act out '8 cookies, eat 3' with counters and write 8 − 3 = 5.

days.title: Hide and find
days.work: Hide some of 7 counters under a cup; tell how many are hidden and write the subtraction.

days.title: Count back
days.work: Subtract 1, 2, or 3 by counting back on a number line.

days.title: Take apart
days.work: Solve '9 kids, 4 are girls, how many boys?' with drawings.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Mixed add/subtract story problems; explain one strategy aloud.

weeks.assessment: Mixed operation story problems and verbal explanation.

objectives: Compare quantities within 20
Solve compare problems

days.title: More or fewer
days.work: Build two cube towers (9 and 6) and tell which has more and how many more.

days.title: Compare stories
days.work: Solve 'Ana has 7 stickers, Ben has 4. How many more does Ana have?' with cube towers.

days.title: Number games
days.work: Play 'War' with cards 0–10 and say who has more and by how much.

days.title: Count to 20 and back
days.work: Count forward and backward from 20; fill in missing numbers on a number path.

days.title: Unit 1 check
days.work: Unit test: counting, writing numerals, add/subtract and compare stories within 10.

objectives: Find all pairs that make 10
Decompose numbers within 10

days.title: Ten-frame partners
days.work: Fill a ten-frame with two colors in every way and record 1+9, 2+8 ... 9+1.

days.title: Go Fish for 10
days.work: Play Go Fish asking for the card that makes 10 with yours.

days.title: Partners of 7 and 8
days.work: Break 7 and 8 into parts with counters; record number bonds.

days.title: Missing part
days.work: Solve 6 + ? = 10 and ? + 3 = 8 using a ten-frame.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make-10 fluency check (1 minute) and number bond worksheet.

weeks.assessment: Make-10 fluency check and number bonds.

objectives: Know doubles facts to 10
Use doubles to solve near doubles

days.title: Doubles
days.work: Use a mirror with counters to see doubles (3 + 3, 4 + 4, 5 + 5); write facts.

days.title: Doubles in life
days.work: Find doubles in real life (egg carton 6 + 6, legs of a spider 4 + 4) and draw them.

days.title: Doubles plus one
days.work: Solve 4 + 5 by thinking 4 + 4 + 1; practice with dominoes.

days.title: Turn-around facts
days.work: Show 2 + 7 and 7 + 2 with cubes and explain why the sum is the same.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Doubles and near-doubles quiz; roll-two-dice game recording sums.

weeks.topic: Relating addition and subtraction; fact families
objectives: Use addition to solve subtraction
Write fact families

days.title: Think addition
days.work: Solve 9 − 4 by asking '4 + ? = 9' with cubes.

days.title: Fact families
days.work: Write the four facts for 3, 5, 8 using a triangle card.

days.title: Missing number
days.work: Solve 8 − ? = 5 and ? − 2 = 6 with a number line.

days.title: Fact family game
days.work: Cover one corner of a triangle card and name the hidden number.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Fact family worksheet (5 families) and missing-number equations.

objectives: Demonstrate fluency for addition and subtraction within 10

days.title: Strategy sort
days.work: Sort fact cards by strategy: count on, doubles, make 10, think addition.

days.title: Number rack
days.work: Use the virtual number rack app to show facts within 10 in one push.

days.title: Roll and solve
days.work: Roll two dice, add, then subtract the smaller from the larger; record 10 rounds.

days.title: Fact practice
days.work: Play Khan Academy 'add and subtract within 10' practice.

days.title: Unit 2 check
days.work: Timed fluency check within 10 (goal: 30 facts in 2 minutes) and written unit test.

weeks.topic: The equal sign and true/false equations
objectives: Explain that = means 'the same as'
Decide whether equations are true or false

days.title: Balance
days.work: Put 4 + 2 cubes on one side and 6 on the other of a hanger balance; discuss 'the same as'.

days.title: True or false
days.work: Decide if 6 = 6, 7 = 8 − 1, 5 + 2 = 2 + 5, 4 + 1 = 5 + 2 are true; prove with cubes.

days.title: Both sides
days.work: Solve 3 + 4 = ? + 5 with cubes.

days.title: Write your own
days.work: Write 3 true and 2 false equations for a family member to sort.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: True/false equations quiz (10 items).

objectives: Solve add-to and take-from problems with unknown change or start
Use a symbol for the unknown

days.title: Unknown change
days.work: Solve 'There were 5 ducks. Some more came. Now there are 9.' with counters and 5 + ? = 9.

days.title: Unknown start
days.work: Solve 'Some fish were in a bowl. 3 more were added. Now there are 8.' with ? + 3 = 8.

days.title: Take from unknowns
days.work: Solve '10 balloons, some popped, 6 left' with drawings.

days.title: Write a story
days.work: Write a story problem for 7 − ? = 4 and solve it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Story problem set with unknowns in all positions (6 items).

objectives: Solve compare problems with bigger/smaller unknown
Add three numbers

days.title: Compare bigger unknown
days.work: Solve 'Leo has 4 shells. Mia has 3 more than Leo.' using cube trains.

days.title: Compare smaller unknown
days.work: Solve 'Mia has 9 rocks; Leo has 2 fewer.'

days.title: Three addends warm-up
days.work: Roll 3 dice and add, looking for a make-10 or double first.

days.title: Problem solving
days.work: Mixed story problems; draw a model for each before writing the equation.

days.title: Unit 3 check
days.work: Unit test on story problems and equal sign.

objectives: Use make-ten to add 8 + 5, 9 + 6
Understand teen numbers as 10 and some ones

days.title: Teen numbers
days.work: Show 13 as 10 + 3 on a double ten-frame; do this for 11–19.

days.title: Make ten
days.work: Solve 9 + 4 by moving 1 counter to make 10 + 3.

days.title: 8 plus
days.work: Solve 8 + 5, 8 + 6, 8 + 7 by making ten; record your thinking.

days.title: Practice game
days.work: Play 'Make Ten and Go' with cards; explain moves aloud.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: 10 make-ten problems with drawings.

objectives: Use doubles to 20
Add three numbers using properties

days.title: Big doubles
days.work: Learn 6+6 through 10+10 with egg cartons and ten-frames.

days.title: Near doubles
days.work: Solve 7 + 8 as 7 + 7 + 1; play a near-doubles card game.

days.title: Three addends
days.work: Solve 'Sam saw 4 birds, 6 squirrels, and 3 rabbits'; choose which two to add first.

days.title: Change the order
days.work: Show 5 + 2 + 5 = 5 + 5 + 2 and explain why it helps.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Doubles to 20 quiz and three-addend word problems.

objectives: Subtract by making ten or thinking addition

days.title: Take to ten
days.work: Solve 13 − 4 as 13 − 3 − 1 on a ten-frame.

days.title: Think addition
days.work: Solve 15 − 7 by thinking 7 + ? = 15.

days.title: Number line jumps
days.work: Show 16 − 9 with jumps on a number line.

days.title: Story problems
days.work: Solve 5 subtraction stories within 20 with a model.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Subtraction strategies quiz; explain a strategy for 14 − 6.

objectives: Solve all problem types within 20
Explain strategies

days.title: Problem types
days.work: Solve one of each: add to, take from, put together, compare within 20.

days.title: Math talk
days.work: Solve 'How many ways can you make 15?' and explain to a family member.

days.title: Fact practice
days.work: Khan Academy 'add and subtract within 20' practice set.

days.title: Create problems
days.work: Write and illustrate two story problems for someone else to solve.

days.title: Unit 4 check
days.work: Unit test: facts and story problems within 20.

objectives: Sort objects into up to three categories
Represent data in a tally chart and picture graph

days.title: Sort it
days.work: Sort a bag of buttons by color, then by number of holes; name your categories.

days.title: Tally
days.work: Record sorted buttons with tally marks in a three-row chart.

days.title: Picture graph
days.work: Make a picture graph of favorite fruits from a family survey (3 choices).

days.title: Ask questions
days.work: Write questions about the graph: how many in all? how many more chose apples than bananas?

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Read a given graph and answer 5 questions.

Interpret data to answer comparison questions

days.title: Plan a survey

days.title: Bar graph
days.work: Turn tallies into a bar graph on grid paper with labels.

days.title: Interpret
days.work: Write 3 statements and 2 how-many-more questions about your graph.

days.title: Unit 5 check
days.work: Present your survey graph to family, then complete a data assessment reading a 3-category graph.

objectives: Count, read and write numbers to 120

days.title: Count by ones

days.work: Color columns and rows on the 120 chart; describe what changes and what stays the same.

days.title: Missing numbers
days.work: Fill in missing numbers on chart pieces (puzzle cut-outs).

days.title: Count large collections

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write numbers 1–120 from a starting point; fill-in chart pieces.

objectives: Understand 10 as a bundle of ten ones

days.title: Bundle ten

days.title: Decade numbers
days.work: Show 10, 20 ... 90 as 1 to 9 tens.

days.title: Build numbers
days.work: Build 34, 58, 71 with base-ten blocks; write tens and ones.

days.title: Different ways
days.work: Show 25 as 2 tens 5 ones and as 1 ten 15 ones.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Place value mat quiz (10 numbers).

weeks.topic: Teen numbers and two-digit numbers in expanded form
objectives: Show 11–19 as a ten and some ones

days.title: Teens
days.work: Build 11–19 and say 'one ten and ___ ones'.

days.title: Expanded form
days.work: Write 47 = 40 + 7; play a match game with cards.

courses.subject: SCI
courses.title: Science 1 (NGSS)
courses.description: First-grade science follows the California NGSS: students investigate how vibrations make sound and how light lets us see, cast shadows, and pass through materials, then design devices that communicate with light and sound. They track patterns of the sun, moon, stars and daylight, explore how plant and animal parts help them survive (and inspire human inventions), and compare parents and offspring. Every unit includes hands-on investigations with household materials and simple engineering design challenges.
courses.framework: California Next Generation Science Standards; 2016 CA Science Framework

standards.1-PS4-1: Plan and conduct investigations to provide evidence that vibrating materials can make sound and that sound can make materials vibrate.
standards.1-PS4-2: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account that objects in darkness can be seen only when illuminated.
standards.1-PS4-3: Plan and conduct investigations to determine the effect of placing objects made with different materials in the path of a beam of light.
standards.1-PS4-4: Use tools and materials to design and build a device that uses light or sound to solve the problem of communicating over a distance.
standards.1-LS1-1: Use materials to design a solution to a human problem by mimicking how plants and/or animals use their external parts to help them survive, grow, and meet their needs.
standards.1-LS1-2: Read texts and use media to determine patterns in behavior of parents and offspring that help offspring survive.
standards.1-LS3-1: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account that young plants and animals are like, but not exactly like, their parents.
standards.1-ESS1-1: Use observations of the sun, moon, and stars to describe patterns that can be predicted.
standards.1-ESS1-2: Make observations at different times of year to relate the amount of daylight to the time of year.
standards.K-2-ETS1-1: Ask questions, make observations, and gather information about a situation people want to change to define a simple problem that can be solved through a new or improved object or tool.
standards.K-2-ETS1-2: Develop a simple sketch, drawing, or physical model to illustrate how the shape of an object helps it function as needed to solve a given problem.
standards.K-2-ETS1-3: Analyze data from tests of two objects designed to solve the same problem to compare the strengths and weaknesses of how each performs.

units.title: Light, Darkness and Shadows

weeks.topic: What scientists do: observing and asking questions

days.work: Observe a leaf, rock and shell with a magnifying glass; draw and label details you couldn't see before.

weeks.topic: What engineers do: defining problems and designing

days.title: Define the problem

objectives: Test two designs and compare data

days.title: Test

weeks.topic: The sun's path across the sky
