weeks.topic: Animal external parts and their jobs
objectives: Identify animal parts and how they help animals survive
materials: rice, gummy worms, water in a cup, marbles

days.title: Parts and jobs
days.work: Match photos of claws, beaks, shells, fins and ears to the job each does (grab, eat, protect, swim, hear).

days.title: Bird beak lab
days.work: Use tweezers, a clothespin, a spoon and chopsticks as 'beaks' to pick up rice, gummy worms and marbles; record which beak works best for each food.

days.title: Protection parts
days.work: Compare photos of a turtle shell, porcupine quills and an armadillo; tell how each part protects the animal.

days.title: Moving parts
days.work: Compare fins, wings, flippers and legs; act out how each animal moves and say what part helps.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw an animal, label 3 external parts and write what each does.

weeks.topic: Plant external parts and their jobs
objectives: Identify plant parts and how they help plants survive

days.title: Plant dissection
days.work: Take apart a weed or flower and tape roots, stem, leaves and flower onto paper with labels.

days.title: Celery lab
days.work: Put a celery stalk in blue-colored water; check after 4 hours and next morning to see how the stem carries water.

days.title: Root pull
days.work: Pull up a weed and a grass clump; compare roots and explain how roots hold plants and take in water.

days.title: Plant protection
days.work: Look closely (safely) at rose thorns or cactus spines and discuss how they protect the plant from animals.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Plant-parts quiz: label a diagram and match each part to its job.

objectives: Identify human inventions inspired by plant and animal parts
Define a problem to solve

days.title: Velcro and burrs
days.work: Compare Velcro and a burr under a magnifier; draw the tiny hooks on both.

days.title: Invention match
days.work: Match inventions (bike helmet, swim fins, sun hat, tweezers) to the animal or plant part they copy (turtle shell, duck feet, leaves, bird beak).

days.title: Define a problem
days.work: Choose a human problem: keeping your head safe, staying cool in the sun, or picking up tiny things; draw the problem.

days.title: Brainstorm
days.work: List animal or plant parts that solve a similar problem in nature for your chosen problem.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain one biomimicry example in two sentences: the nature part and the invention.

objectives: Sketch and build a solution that mimics a plant or animal part
materials: cardboard, tape, foil, sponges, paper plates

days.title: Two sketches
days.work: Sketch two designs for your problem inspired by an animal or plant part (e.g., a shell-shaped egg protector).

days.title: Choose and plan
days.work: Choose one design and list materials you need; explain why its shape will work.

days.title: Build
days.work: Build the prototype from household materials.

days.title: Label
days.work: Label the prototype's parts and write which nature part each copies.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present the prototype to family and use a 4-item design checklist to self-check.

objectives: Test two designs and compare results
Improve a design using data

days.title: Test design A
days.work: Run 3 trials with your first design (e.g., drop the protected egg from 30 cm, 60 cm, 90 cm) and record results.

days.title: Test design B
days.work: Build a quick version of your second sketch and run the same 3 trials.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Make a T-chart of strengths and weaknesses for each design using your data.

days.title: Improve
days.work: Change one thing on the better design and test it again.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write or dictate what you changed, why, and whether the data improved.

weeks.assessment: Test data table and improvement reflection.

objectives: Explain how plants and animals use external parts to survive and inspire inventions

days.title: Mystery Science
days.work: Watch a free Mystery Science animal-parts or plant-parts lesson and answer the mystery question.

days.title: Backyard field guide
days.work: Find 4 plants or animals outside (birds, insects, weeds) and draw each with one labeled survival part.

days.title: Guess the animal
days.work: Play 'Guess the animal from its parts' with a family member using clues like 'webbed feet and a flat bill'.

days.title: Share the guide
days.work: Present your field guide and explain one part that could inspire a new invention.

days.title: Unit 6 check
days.work: Assessment: match parts to functions and explain one biomimicry design.

weeks.topic: How animal parents care for their young
objectives: Identify parent behaviors that help offspring survive
materials: 'Are You My Mother?' by P.D. Eastman (library)
PBS LearningMedia Wild Kratts or nature clips

days.title: Read Are You My Mother?
days.work: Read the story and list what the baby bird needs from its mother.

days.title: Penguin parents
days.work: Watch a PBS clip of emperor penguins and list 3 ways parents keep chicks warm and fed.

days.title: Feeding young
days.work: Compare how birds (bring worms), mammals (milk) and some fish (guard eggs) care for young on a chart.

days.title: Protecting young
days.work: Read about kangaroo pouches and crocodiles carrying babies in their mouths; draw one.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Sort 12 behavior cards into feed, protect, keep warm, or teach.

weeks.topic: How young animals help themselves survive
objectives: Identify offspring behaviors that signal needs or keep them safe
materials: 'Make Way for Ducklings' by Robert McCloskey (library)

days.title: Calling for help
days.work: Listen to recordings (PBS or library) of baby birds chirping and kittens mewing; tell what each baby is asking for.

days.title: Follow the leader
days.work: Read 'Make Way for Ducklings' and explain why the ducklings stay in a line behind their mother.

days.title: Learning by copying
days.work: Read about bear cubs and young chimpanzees learning to find food by watching parents.

days.title: Interview
days.work: Interview a parent about how you signaled your needs as a baby and how they responded; record 3 answers.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain one offspring behavior and how it helps the baby survive, in two sentences.

weeks.topic: Patterns in parent and offspring behavior
objectives: Find patterns across many kinds of animals

days.title: Pattern chart
days.work: Make a chart of 6 animals with columns for 'what parents do' and 'what babies do'.

days.title: Find patterns
days.work: Circle behaviors that appear for many animals (feeding, protecting, calling) and state one pattern.

days.title: Mini-book draft
days.work: Write a 4-page mini-book about one animal family (e.g., robins) with a fact on each page.

days.title: Share
days.work: Read your mini-book aloud and answer two questions from a listener.

days.title: Unit 7 check
days.work: Assessment: read a short passage about a new animal and identify parent and offspring behaviors.

weeks.topic: Young animals are like their parents
objectives: Compare traits of young animals and their parents

days.title: Match the families
days.work: Match 10 baby animal photos to their parents and name one trait that gave it away.

days.title: Puppy and dog Venn
days.work: Compare a puppy and its parent in a Venn diagram: ears, fur color, size, tail.

days.title: Not exactly alike
days.work: Look at a photo of a litter of kittens and list differences between the kittens and their mother.

days.title: Family photos
days.work: Compare photos of yourself, siblings and parents; find 2 shared traits and 2 differences.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write 'Young animals are like their parents because... but not exactly because...' with evidence.

weeks.topic: Young plants are like their parents
objectives: Compare young plants with parent plants
Measure variation
materials: adult plant of the same kind (or photo)

days.title: Seedling vs. adult
days.work: Compare bean seedlings with an adult bean plant photo; list matching leaf shapes and differences in size.

days.title: Measure leaves
days.work: Measure the longest leaf on 5 seedlings in centimeters and record the results.

days.title: Same kind of flower
days.work: Compare 3 flowers from the same plant type (e.g., roses or dandelions); note color and petal differences.

days.title: Plant journal
days.work: Draw and label two seedlings side by side showing how they are alike and different.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an evidence statement about plants being like, but not exactly like, their parents.

weeks.topic: Variation within a kind of animal or plant
objectives: Describe how individuals of the same kind vary

days.title: Dog breeds
days.work: Compare photos of a Chihuahua and a Great Dane; list what makes both dogs and what is different.

days.title: Leaf collection
days.work: Collect 10 leaves from one tree and measure each length with paper clips.

days.title: Leaf graph
days.work: Graph leaf lengths into short, medium and long groups.

days.title: Discuss
days.work: Discuss why leaves on one tree and puppies in one litter are not exactly the same.

days.title: Unit 8 check
days.work: Assessment: compare a parent and offspring picture and explain likenesses and differences.

objectives: Apply science ideas from the year to design a solution
materials: cups, string, flashlight, cardboard, tape, foil

days.title: Choose a problem
days.work: Choose a challenge: send a message across the yard using light or sound, or solve a human problem by copying an animal part.

days.title: Sketch and build
days.work: Sketch two ideas, choose one and build a first prototype.

days.title: Test
days.work: Test the prototype 3 times and record what happened in a simple data table.

days.title: Improve
days.work: Change one feature based on your data and test again.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Get feedback from a family member using 'one thing that works, one thing to try'.

objectives: Communicate results and reflect on a year of investigations

days.title: Notebook review
days.work: Page through your science notebook and flag your 3 favorite investigations.

days.title: Poster
days.work: Make a poster for your showcase project: problem, design sketch, test data and improvement.

days.title: Science fair
days.work: Present the project and one favorite investigation to family, answering their questions.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write or dictate 3 sentences about what you learned about sound, light, sky or living things.

days.title: Year-end check
days.work: Complete a year-end science review of key ideas from each unit.

weeks.assessment: Science fair presentation and year-end review.

courses.subject: HSS
courses.title: A Child's Place in Time and Space
courses.description: Grade 1 History–Social Science helps children understand their place in the world: rules and fair play, direct and representative democracy, maps and globes, American symbols, documents and holidays, how life has changed over time, the contributions of American Indians and immigrants, and basic economics of work, goods, services and money. Students analyze historic photographs and documents from the Library of Congress, National Archives and Calisphere and conduct an oral-history interview.
courses.framework: California History–Social Science Content Standards; 2016 CA History–Social Science Framework

standards.1.1: Students describe the rights and individual responsibilities of citizenship.
standards.1.1.1: Understand the rule-making process in a direct democracy (everyone votes on the rules) and in a representative democracy (an elected group makes the rules), with examples from classroom, school and community.
standards.1.1.2: Understand fair play, good sportsmanship, respect for the rights and opinions of others, and respect for rules, including the meaning of the Golden Rule.
standards.1.2.1: Locate on maps and globes their local community, California, the United States, the seven continents, and the four oceans.
standards.1.2.2: Compare the information from a three-dimensional model to the information from a picture of the same location.
standards.1.2.3: Construct a simple map, using cardinal directions and map symbols.
standards.1.2.4: Describe how location, weather, and physical environment affect the way people live (food, clothing, shelter, transportation, recreation).
standards.1.3.1: Recite the Pledge of Allegiance and sing songs that express American ideals (e.g., 'My Country 'Tis of Thee').
standards.1.3.2: Understand the significance of national holidays and the heroism and achievements of the people associated with them.
standards.1.3.3: Identify American symbols, landmarks, and essential documents (flag, bald eagle, Statue of Liberty, U.S. Constitution, Declaration of Independence) and the people and events associated with them.
standards.1.4.1: Examine the structure of schools and communities in the past.
standards.1.4.2: Study transportation methods of earlier days.
standards.1.4.3: Recognize similarities and differences of earlier generations in work, dress, manners, stories, games, and festivals, drawing from biographies, oral histories, and folklore.
standards.1.5.1: Recognize that they are all part of the same community, sharing principles, goals and traditions despite varied ancestry; the forms, benefits and challenges of diversity.
standards.1.5.2: Understand the ways in which American Indians and immigrants have helped define Californian and American culture.
standards.1.5.3: Compare the beliefs, customs, ceremonies, traditions, and social practices of varied cultures, drawing from folklore.
standards.1.6.1: Understand the concept of exchange and the use of money to purchase goods and services.
standards.1.6.2: Identify the specialized work people do to manufacture, transport, and market goods and services, and the contributions of those who work in the home.

resources.name: Library of Congress – Free to Use and Reuse photo sets
resources.note: Historic photos of schools, transportation, work and holidays for primary-source analysis

resources.name: National Archives DocsTeach
resources.note: Primary-source activities including the Declaration of Independence and Constitution

resources.name: Calisphere
resources.note: California historical photographs: one-room schools, early towns, Native Californian baskets, Angel Island

resources.name: Smithsonian Learning Lab
resources.note: Collections on American symbols, Native cultures and everyday life long ago

resources.name: PBS LearningMedia – Social Studies
resources.note: Short videos on communities, maps, holidays and jobs

units.title: Rules, Fairness and Good Citizenship
units.big_idea: Rules help us live and learn together, and good citizens treat others fairly.

units.title: Maps, Globes and Where We Live
units.big_idea: Maps and globes show where places are, and where we live shapes how we live.

units.title: American Symbols, Holidays and Heroes
units.big_idea: Symbols, songs, documents and holidays remind Americans of shared ideals and the people who worked for them.

units.title: Then and Now: Schools, Communities, Transportation and Families
units.big_idea: Life has changed in many ways over time, but some things stay the same.

units.title: Many Cultures, One Community
units.big_idea: People of many backgrounds, including American Indians and immigrants, have shaped California and America.

units.title: Work, Goods, Services and Money
units.big_idea: People work at different jobs to make, move, and sell goods and services, and we use money to exchange.

objectives: Explain why rules are needed at home, school and in the community
materials: picture cards of community signs (stop sign, crosswalk, library 'quiet')

days.title: No-rules game
days.work: Play a board game with no rules for two minutes, then talk about what went wrong and why rules matter.

days.title: Rules around us
days.work: Walk the neighborhood and photograph or draw 5 signs that show rules (stop sign, crosswalk, park rules); tell what each keeps safe.

days.title: Home rules chart
days.work: Work with family to write 5 homeschool rules on chart paper; draw a picture for each.

days.title: Rights and responsibilities
days.work: Read 'What If Everybody Did That?' (Ellen Javernick, library) and match 3 rights with 3 responsibilities.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain one home rule and one community rule and what could happen without each.

weeks.assessment: Oral explanation of two rules and their purpose.

weeks.topic: The Golden Rule and respecting others
objectives: State the Golden Rule in your own words
Show respect for others' rights and opinions

days.title: Golden Rule
days.work: Read 'The Golden Rule' by Ilene Cooper and say the rule in your own words.

days.title: Role-play
days.work: Act out 4 situations (someone cuts in line, a friend is left out) and show a Golden Rule choice.

days.title: Different opinions
days.work: Survey family on a favorite food; practice saying 'I see it differently because...' politely.

days.title: Kindness log
days.work: Do and record 3 kind acts this week, drawing each in a kindness log.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw a comic strip showing someone following the Golden Rule and explain it.

weeks.assessment: Golden Rule comic strip with explanation.

objectives: Describe fair play and good sportsmanship

days.title: What is fair?
days.work: Discuss whether 'fair' always means 'the same'; sort scenario cards into fair and unfair.

days.title: Game day
days.work: Play a backyard game and practice taking turns, following rules and shaking hands at the end.

days.title: Winning and losing
days.work: Role-play good and poor ways to win and lose; make a T-chart of sportsmanlike words.

days.title: Team pledge
days.work: Write a 3-line good-sport pledge and sign it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Tell how a good sport acts in a game you played this week.

objectives: Explain direct democracy and vote on a family decision

days.title: What is voting?
days.work: Read 'Duck for President' by Doreen Cronin (library) and talk about why the animals voted.

days.title: Family vote
days.work: Hold a direct vote on Friday's family movie or snack with paper ballots; count the tallies.

days.title: Majority rules
days.work: Count votes and explain that the choice with the most votes wins; discuss how the others feel.

days.title: Make a rule by vote
days.work: Propose a new household rule and let everyone vote on it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain direct democracy in one sentence and give the family-vote example.

weeks.assessment: Explanation of direct democracy with an example.

objectives: Explain representative democracy with community examples
materials: local city council website or newspaper

days.title: Representatives
days.work: Learn that people elect a small group (city council, mayor) to make rules for many people.

days.title: Our leaders
days.work: Look up your city's mayor and city council members and find one rule (law) they made.

days.title: Mock election
days.work: Make campaign posters for two stuffed-animal candidates and have family elect a 'family representative'.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Make a T-chart comparing direct democracy (everyone votes on rules) and representative democracy (leaders make rules).

days.title: Unit 1 check
days.work: Assessment: sort examples into direct or representative democracy and explain the Golden Rule.

weeks.topic: What is a map? Models vs. pictures
objectives: Compare a 3-D model and a picture of the same place

days.title: Bird's-eye view
days.work: Look down at a toy from above and from the side; draw both views.

days.title: Room model
days.work: Build a 3-D model of your bedroom with blocks and small boxes.

days.title: Photo vs. model
days.work: Photograph your room and compare: what does the model show that the photo doesn't (and vice versa)?

days.title: First map
days.work: Draw a bird's-eye map of your room with simple symbols.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain one thing a model shows better and one thing a picture shows better.

weeks.topic: Map symbols, keys and cardinal directions
objectives: Use map keys and cardinal directions
materials: sticky notes labeled N, S, E, W

days.title: Directions in the house
days.work: Label walls N, S, E, W using a compass; follow directions like 'take 3 steps north'.

days.title: Map key
days.work: Study a park map's key and find 5 symbols on the map.

days.title: Compass rose
days.work: Draw a compass rose and add it to your room map.

days.title: Treasure hunt
days.work: Follow a family-made map with symbols and directions to find a hidden treasure.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make a map of your yard or street with a key of 4 symbols and a compass rose.

weeks.assessment: Yard or street map with key and compass rose.

objectives: Construct a map of the local community

days.title: Walking tour
days.work: Walk your neighborhood and list landmarks (library, park, store, fire station).

days.title: Street map
days.work: Find your home on a printed street map or online map of your town.

days.title: Draw the community
days.work: Draw a community map with your home, 4 landmarks, a key and a compass rose.

days.title: Routes
days.work: Draw a route from home to the library and describe it using north, south, east, west.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Give a family member directions to a landmark using your map.

weeks.assessment: Community map with key and route directions.

weeks.topic: California and the United States on maps
objectives: Locate your community, California and the U.S. on maps and a globe

days.title: Nested places
days.work: Make nesting circles: home → city → California → United States → North America → Earth.

days.title: California map
days.work: Find your city, Sacramento (the capital) and the Pacific Ocean on a California map.

days.title: U.S. map
days.work: Find California on a U.S. map; name the states that border it (Oregon, Nevada, Arizona).

days.title: Globe find
days.work: Find the United States and California on a globe; compare the globe to a flat map.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Label your city, California and the U.S. on blank maps.

objectives: Locate the seven continents and four major oceans

days.title: Continents song
days.work: Learn a continents song and point to each continent on the globe.

days.title: Oceans
days.work: Find the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian and Arctic Oceans; trace them with a finger.

days.title: Puzzle map
days.work: Cut out continent shapes and glue them on a blue world map in the right places.

days.title: Animal travel
days.work: Place animal pictures on their continents (kangaroo → Australia, penguin → Antarctica).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Label 7 continents and 4 oceans on a blank world map.

weeks.topic: How place shapes the way people live
objectives: Describe how weather and environment affect food, clothing, shelter, transportation, recreation
materials: photos of homes around the world (igloo, stilt house, adobe)
Library of Congress or Smithsonian images

days.title: Homes around the world
days.work: Compare photos of an igloo, stilt house, adobe and apartment; tell how each fits its environment.

days.title: Clothing and weather
days.work: Sort clothing cards for snowy, rainy, hot and desert places.

days.title: California places
days.work: Compare life at the beach, in the Sierra Nevada mountains and in the desert (food, clothing, fun).

days.title: Getting around
days.work: Compare transportation in snowy places (snowmobile), islands (boats) and cities (trains).

days.title: Unit 2 check
days.work: Assessment: locate places on maps and explain how one environment affects people's lives.

weeks.topic: The Pledge of Allegiance and patriotic songs
objectives: Recite the Pledge and explain its key words
Sing songs that express American ideals
materials: lyrics to 'My Country 'Tis of Thee' and 'America the Beautiful'

days.title: The Pledge
days.work: Read the Pledge of Allegiance line by line and discuss what allegiance, liberty and justice mean.

days.title: Words to pictures
days.work: Draw a picture for each key word (liberty, justice, indivisible).

days.title: My Country 'Tis of Thee
days.work: Learn the first verse and talk about 'sweet land of liberty'.

days.title: America the Beautiful
days.work: Learn the first verse and match lines ('purple mountain majesties') to photos of American landscapes.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Recite the Pledge and sing one song; explain one idea it expresses.

weeks.assessment: Recitation and explanation of one key word.

objectives: Explain why we celebrate Veterans Day and Thanksgiving
materials: Library of Congress photos of veterans
'Thank You, Sarah' by Laurie Halse Anderson (library)

days.title: Veterans Day
days.work: Learn what a veteran is and why we honor them on November 11; look at Library of Congress photos of veterans.

days.title: Thank-you card
days.work: Write a thank-you card to a veteran (family member or local VA).

days.title: Thanksgiving history
days.work: Learn about the 1621 harvest feast of the Wampanoag and the Pilgrims from a children's nonfiction book.

days.title: Sarah Hale
days.work: Read 'Thank You, Sarah' and learn how Sarah Josepha Hale helped make Thanksgiving a national holiday.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make a two-panel poster explaining Veterans Day and Thanksgiving.

objectives: Identify the flag, bald eagle, Statue of Liberty, Liberty Bell and their meanings

days.title: The flag
days.work: Count the stars and stripes and learn what they stand for; make a paper flag.

days.title: Bald eagle
days.work: Learn why the bald eagle was chosen as the national bird; view it on the Great Seal and a quarter.

days.title: Statue of Liberty
days.work: Look at historic Library of Congress photos of the Statue of Liberty being built; discuss what it welcomes.

days.title: Liberty Bell
days.work: Find the crack in a Liberty Bell photo and learn its story.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Match 6 symbols to their names and meanings.

weeks.topic: Essential documents: Declaration of Independence and Constitution
objectives: Identify key documents and the people connected to them
materials: National Archives DocsTeach images of the Declaration and Constitution

days.title: Look closely
days.work: Examine an image of the Declaration of Independence (National Archives) with a magnifier; find John Hancock's signature.

days.title: July 4th
days.work: Learn that the Declaration said America would be free and that we celebrate on Independence Day.

days.title: We the People
days.work: Look at the first words of the Constitution and discuss that it is the nation's rulebook.

days.title: Class constitution
days.work: Write a 'family constitution' with 3 rules everyone signs.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain what each document is and name one person connected to it (Jefferson, Washington).

weeks.topic: Heroes behind our holidays: Martin Luther King Jr.
objectives: Explain the achievements of Dr. King and why we honor him
materials: LOC photo of the 1963 March on Washington

days.title: Read
days.work: Read 'Martin's Big Words' and list 3 'big words' Dr. King used.

days.title: Primary source
days.work: Look at a Library of Congress photo of the 1963 March on Washington; describe what you see and wonder.

days.title: Dream cloud
days.work: Write and illustrate your own dream for a fairer world.

days.title: Peaceful problem-solving
days.work: Role-play solving a disagreement with words, like Dr. King taught.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Tell why we celebrate Martin Luther King Jr. Day in January and name one thing Dr. King worked for.

objectives: Explain the achievements of George Washington and Abraham Lincoln
materials: portraits from the Library of Congress

days.title: George Washington
days.work: Read a picture biography and list 2 facts; find him on the quarter and dollar bill.

days.title: Abraham Lincoln
days.work: Read a picture biography and learn why he was called 'Honest Abe'; find him on the penny.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare Washington and Lincoln on a Venn diagram.

days.title: Landmarks
days.work: Look at photos of the Washington Monument and Lincoln Memorial and match them to each president.

days.title: Unit 3 check
days.work: Assessment: symbols, documents, holidays and heroes.

objectives: Compare schools in the past and present using primary sources

days.title: Photo detective
days.work: Study a Library of Congress photo of a one-room schoolhouse: what do you see, think, wonder?

days.title: Slate lesson
days.work: Do today's spelling on a slate like children long ago; discuss what it would be like with no paper.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Make a then-and-now chart (desks, lunch, subjects, getting to school).

days.title: Read
days.work: Read a picture book about school long ago (e.g., 'Going to School in 1876' or similar from the library).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw yourself at school then and now with 3 labeled differences.

objectives: Examine how communities looked and worked in the past
materials: Calisphere photos of your area or a California town in the 1900s

days.title: Old town photo
days.work: Look at Calisphere photos of a California main street around 1900; list what is the same and different today.

days.title: Jobs then
days.work: Learn about the general store, blacksmith and milkman.

days.title: Our town's past
days.work: Find a historic photo of your own town (Calisphere or local library) and compare it with today.

days.title: Model town
days.work: Build a 'long ago' main street from boxes with 3 buildings.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain 2 ways communities have changed and 1 way they stayed the same.

weeks.assessment: Oral comparison with evidence from photos.

objectives: Describe and compare transportation long ago and today
materials: LOC photos of wagons, trains, early cars

days.title: Photo sort
days.work: Sort Library of Congress photos of transportation (stagecoach, steam train, Model T, airplane) from oldest to newest.

days.title: Timeline
days.work: Create a transportation timeline with drawings.

days.title: Then and now
days.work: Compare a trip to San Francisco by stagecoach vs. car (time, comfort).

days.title: Build a vehicle
days.work: Build a wagon or train from recycled materials.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain how one invention changed how people travel.

weeks.topic: Family life and work long ago
objectives: Compare work at home and outside the home across generations

days.title: Chores then
days.work: Look at photos of washing clothes on a washboard and churning butter; try shaking cream into butter in a jar.

days.title: Chores now
days.work: List appliances that do those jobs today.

days.title: Jobs outside
days.work: Compare jobs of grandparents' generation with jobs today.

days.title: Read
days.work: Read 'Ox-Cart Man' by Donald Hall (library) and list the family's work through the year.

courses.subject: VAPA
courses.title: Art & Music 1
courses.description: Art & Music 1 combines visual art and general music. Students explore line, shape, color, texture, pattern and form through drawing, painting, collage, printmaking and clay, looking closely at works by Kandinsky, Matisse, Eric Carle, Hokusai, Van Gogh and O'Keeffe and at art from many cultures. In music they keep a steady beat, read simple rhythms (ta, ti-ti, rest), sing sol-mi melodies and folk songs, identify instrument families, and respond to dynamics and tempo in pieces such as 'Peter and the Wolf' and 'Carnival of the Animals', ending the year with an art show and concert.

units.title: Lines and Shapes / Steady Beat
units.big_idea: Artists use lines and shapes to make pictures; music has a steady heartbeat we can feel and move to.

units.title: Color and Mood / Rhythm: Long and Short Sounds
units.big_idea: Colors can show feelings; rhythms are patterns of long and short sounds we can read and write.

units.title: Texture and Collage / High and Low: Pitch and Melody
units.big_idea: Texture is how things feel or look like they feel; melodies move up, down and stay the same.

units.title: Pattern and Printmaking / Songs of the Season and Folk Songs
units.big_idea: Repeating patterns make art and music; songs carry traditions from many places.

units.title: Form and Sculpture / Instruments and Timbre
units.big_idea: Form is 3-D art we can walk around; every instrument has its own tone color.

units.title: Art and Music from Many Cultures
units.big_idea: People in different places and times make art and music for many reasons.

units.title: Nature, Animals and Stories / Dynamics and Tempo
units.big_idea: Artists and composers tell stories about nature and animals using color, loud/soft and fast/slow.

units.title: Portfolio, Art Show and Spring Concert
units.big_idea: Artists choose, prepare and share their best work with an audience.

courses.subject: PE
courses.title: PE 1
courses.description: PE 1 builds fundamental movement skills through play: moving safely in space, locomotor skills (hop, gallop, jog, slide, skip), balancing and rolling, throwing, catching, kicking, striking, dribbling, jumping rope and dancing. Children learn how exercise affects the heart, muscles and bones, track simple fitness measures, and practice cooperation and sportsmanship, finishing with a family field day.
courses.framework: California Physical Education Model Content Standards; 2009 CA Physical Education Framework

standards.PE-1.1.1: Balance on one, two, three, four, and five body parts.
standards.PE-1.1.2: Balance while walking forward and sideways on a narrow, elevated surface.
standards.PE-1.1.3: Demonstrate the relationship of under, over, behind, next to, through, right, left, up, down, forward, backward, and in front of using the body and an object.
standards.PE-1.1.4: Create a routine that includes two types of body rolls (log roll, egg roll, rocking-chair roll) and a stationary balance position.
standards.PE-1.1.5: Hop, gallop, jog, and slide using a mature motor pattern.
standards.PE-1.1.6: Jump continuously with a self-turned rope and jump a long rope turned by others.
standards.PE-1.1.7: Toss and throw a ball underhand and overhand toward a target, stepping with the opposite foot.
standards.PE-1.1.8: Catch a gently tossed or bounced ball using the hands.
standards.PE-1.1.9: Kick a stationary and a slowly rolling ball using the inside of the foot.
standards.PE-1.1.10: Strike a balloon or ball upward and forward with the hand or a short-handled paddle.
standards.PE-1.1.11: Dribble a ball continuously with one hand while stationary and moving.
standards.PE-1.1.12: Perform simple rhythmic movement and dance sequences to music.
standards.PE-1.2.1: Explain the difference between pathways (straight, curved, zigzag), levels (high, medium, low), and personal vs. general space.
standards.PE-1.2.2: Describe the critical elements (cues) of the hop, gallop, jog, and slide.
standards.PE-1.2.3: Explain the critical elements of throwing, catching, and kicking (e.g., step with the opposite foot, watch the ball).
standards.PE-1.3.1: Participate in physical activities that are enjoyable and challenging.
standards.PE-1.3.2: Participate in moderate to vigorous physical activity for increasing periods of time.
standards.PE-1.3.3: Demonstrate muscular strength and endurance activities (e.g., modified push-ups, curl-ups, hanging).
standards.PE-1.3.4: Demonstrate flexibility exercises for major muscle groups.
standards.PE-1.3.5: Walk and jog for increasing distances to build aerobic capacity.
standards.PE-1.4.1: Recognize that physical activity makes the heart beat faster and identify the location of the heart.
standards.PE-1.4.2: Explain that the body needs water, healthy food, and rest to be active.
standards.PE-1.4.3: Identify that muscles move bones and that physical activity makes muscles and bones stronger.
standards.PE-1.4.4: Explain why warming up and stretching prepare the body for activity.
standards.PE-1.5.1: Work cooperatively with a partner or small group and share equipment.
standards.PE-1.5.2: Follow rules and safety procedures and take turns during physical activity.
standards.PE-1.5.3: Give positive encouragement to others and accept feedback.
standards.PE-1.5.4: Identify feelings that result from participation in physical activity.

courses.subject: HEALTH
courses.title: Health 1
courses.description: Health 1 teaches young children to understand and care for themselves and others: naming and managing feelings, kindness and conflict resolution, handwashing, tooth care and sleep, MyPlate food groups and healthy snacks, daily physical activity, the senses and major organs, and safety at home, at play and on the road. Students also learn medicine and poison safety and meet community health helpers.
courses.framework: 2008 California Health Education Content Standards; 2019 CA Health Education Framework

standards.H-1.1.1.M: Identify a range of feelings and how they can be expressed in healthy ways.
standards.H-1.1.2.M: Describe ways to show caring, kindness, and respect for others, including people who are different.
standards.H-1.1.3.M: Recognize teasing and bullying behaviors and why they are harmful.
standards.H-1.4.1.M: Use 'I-messages' and listening skills to express needs and feelings and to ask a trusted adult for help.
standards.H-1.4.2.M: Demonstrate simple ways to resolve conflicts with friends and family.
standards.H-1.7.1.M: Practice healthy ways to calm down and manage strong feelings.
standards.H-1.1.1.P: Explain how germs spread and how handwashing and covering coughs prevent illness.
standards.H-1.1.2.P: Describe the importance of caring for teeth, including brushing, flossing, and dental checkups.
standards.H-1.1.3.P: Explain why sleep and rest are important for health.
standards.H-1.3.1.P: Identify health helpers in the community (doctor, nurse, dentist, pharmacist) and how they keep us healthy.
standards.H-1.7.1.P: Demonstrate proper handwashing, toothbrushing, and personal hygiene practices.
standards.H-1.8.1.P: Encourage others to practice healthy habits and to keep the environment clean (reduce, reuse, recycle).
standards.H-1.1.1.N: Classify foods into the food groups shown on MyPlate.
standards.H-1.1.2.N: Explain why the body needs a variety of healthy foods and water.
standards.H-1.1.3.N: Identify healthy snacks and the importance of eating breakfast.
standards.H-1.1.4.N: Describe the benefits of daily physical activity for the heart, muscles, and mood.
standards.H-1.2.1.N: Identify how family, friends, and advertising influence food choices.
standards.H-1.5.1.N: Use a simple decision-making process to choose healthy snacks and drinks.
standards.H-1.6.1.N: Set a short-term goal to eat more fruits and vegetables or be more physically active and track progress.
standards.H-1.7.1.N: Practice healthy eating and food-safety habits (washing hands and produce before eating).
standards.H-1.1.1.G: Identify the five senses and the body parts associated with them.
standards.H-1.1.2.G: Describe how people grow and change over time.
standards.H-1.1.3.G: Identify major body organs (heart, lungs, brain, stomach) and their basic jobs.
standards.H-1.1.1.S: Identify safe practices as a pedestrian, bike rider, and car passenger (crosswalks, helmets, car/booster seats, seat belts).
standards.H-1.1.2.S: Explain fire safety rules, including stop-drop-and-roll and a home escape plan.
standards.H-1.1.3.S: Distinguish safe and unsafe touch and situations, and identify trusted adults.
standards.H-1.1.4.S: Identify water, sun, and playground safety rules.
standards.H-1.4.1.S: Demonstrate how to call 911 and give your name and address in an emergency.
standards.H-1.7.1.S: Practice safety behaviors at home, at play, and on the road.
standards.H-1.1.1.A: Explain that medicines can help or harm and should be given only by trusted adults.
standards.H-1.1.2.A: Identify household products that are harmful if swallowed, touched, or inhaled, and the poison symbol.
standards.H-1.1.3.A: Explain that tobacco smoke and vaping are harmful to the body.
standards.H-1.4.1.A: Demonstrate saying 'no' and telling a trusted adult about unsafe substances.

units.title: My Feelings and My Friends
units.big_idea: All feelings are okay; how we express them and treat others matters.

units.title: Germs, Hygiene and Healthy Habits
units.big_idea: Clean hands, clean teeth and enough sleep keep our bodies healthy.

units.title: Food Groups and Healthy Eating
units.big_idea: Eating a variety of foods from every food group gives our bodies what they need.

units.title: Active Bodies
units.big_idea: Moving every day keeps our heart, muscles and minds strong.

units.big_idea: Our senses and organs work together, and we keep growing and changing.

units.big_idea: Knowing safety rules and trusted adults helps us stay safe at home, at play and on the road.

units.big_idea: Some things can help or harm our bodies; we ask trusted adults before touching or taking anything.
